00076     
00077     inline 
00078     float lookupIndex(const float fIndex) throw()
00079     {
00080         const int iIndex0 = (int)fIndex;
00081         const float* pValue0 = wavetable + iIndex0;
00082         const float value0 = *pValue0;
00083         return value0 + (fIndex - iIndex0) * (*(pValue0+1) - value0);
00084     }
00085

00109 #define Osc_Docs    @param  freq            The fundamental frequency of the wave.                          \
00110                     @param  initialPhase    The phase (0-1) at which the wave should start on creation.     \
00111                                             This may be specified with multiple values using a single       \
00112                                             channel Buffer as an array.
00113 
00114 #define TableOsc_Docs       @param  table               The wavetable to use. This should be a single channel Buffer            \
00115                                                         containing a single cycle of the desired waveform. The size of          \
00116                                                         Buffer is not important (athough larger sizes will generallly           \
00117                                                         result in higher quality) but the Buffer should have an                 \
00118                                                         interpolation sample after the last value. For example, an 8192         \
00119                                                         point Buffer (as used with SinOsc) actually has 8193 values but         \
00120                                                         this is shrunk (using Buffer::shrinkSize()) to a size of 8192 and       \
00121                                                         the value at sample [8192] and sample [0] should be the same.
00122 
00123 #define HarminicOsc_Docs    @param  harmonicWeights     This creates an internal wavetable using a series of sine wave          \
00124                                                         harmonics. The amplitude of these sines is govened by this single       \
00125                                                         channel Buffer. e.g.,                                                   \
00126                                                         @code Buffer(1.0, 0.5, 0.333, 0.25, 0.2, 0.167, 0.143, 0.125) @endcode  \
00127                                                         .. would make a pseudo-sawtooth wave.
